name: HashiCorp Vault
summary: A secret-management service that authenticates clients, authorizes mounted backends, protects durable state behind a security barrier, and expires leased credentials.

features.name: Barrier-protected durable storage
features.description: Vault treats the physical storage backend as untrusted and encrypts data through a security barrier before persistence; the core loads protected mount and auth configuration after unseal.
benefits: Raw backend access does not directly expose stored secrets
Storage backends can provide durability without owning secret semantics
costs: Barrier and seal state add startup and recovery transitions
Storage availability and encryption configuration remain critical dependencies

features.name: Mounted backend and policy routing
features.description: Vault routes authenticated requests through configurable auth methods, policies, and mounted logical or credential backends, allowing backend-specific secret operations behind a common core.
benefits: Separates authentication and authorization from backend implementations
Supports multiple secret engines and auth methods behind one API boundary
costs: Mount paths, policy rules, and backend contracts become operational configuration
Authorization behavior depends on correctly composed policy and mount state

features.name: Leased secret lifecycle
features.description: Secrets and auth responses can carry TTL, maximum TTL, renewable state, and lease identity; expiration management renews or revokes them according to those lifecycle rules.
benefits: Limits credential lifetime and supports automatic revocation
Makes renewal and revocation explicit client operations
costs: Clients must handle renewal, expiration, and revocation failures
Lease tracking adds background state and timing sensitivity

mathematical_views.question: How do initialization, sealing, unsealing, and protected configuration loading constrain which operations are enabled?
assumptions: The barrier key is unavailable while sealed
A valid unseal procedure transitions the core to an operational state
The model abstracts individual seal providers and key custody

mathematical_views.question: How does an authenticated request traverse token identity, policy permissions, mount routing, and a backend operation?
assumptions: Policies define the permitted path/action relation
Audit and replication side effects are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Under what transitions does a leased secret remain renewable, expire, or become revoked?
assumptions: TTL and maximum TTL are authoritative lifecycle bounds
Renewal and revocation operations follow backend contracts
Clock behavior and scheduler delay are abstracted

benefits: Encrypted durable state behind a storage abstraction
costs: Seal custody and unseal availability affect service startup and recovery
Policy and mount configuration increases authorization surface area
Renewal timing and expiration handling complicate clients
